exposure: Birth-related expectation violations (interaction with clinical staff and midwives)
cohort: The study included 125 women who completed two surveys, one during pregnancy and one up to six months postpartum.
finding: Negative expectation violations regarding the mode of birth, along with primiparous status, significantly predicted higher postpartum somatic symptoms and stress.
mod_finding: More negative expectation violations concerning the mode of birth were a significant predictor for higher postpartum somatic symptoms and stress.
